who: Donald W. Giffin, history faculty member and administrator at Maryland; PhD Vanderbilt 1962.

evidence.says: The 1970–1972 university bulletin lists Donald W. Giffin as director of admissions and registrations, with Vanderbilt MA 1956 and PhD 1962.
The obituary describes a Vanderbilt history doctorate and appointment to the University of Maryland History Department in 1963.
The authority identifies Donald W. Giffin through From Scotland to America (2004); it supplies no university affiliation or doctorate.

notes: The supervisor is identifiable, but no source found connects him to the candidate’s genealogical book. Shared name alone is insufficient.

who: Historian of science at UC San Diego; PhD UC Berkeley 1997.

evidence.says: UCSD’s History faculty profile gives a Berkeley PhD in history of science in 1997.
Berkeley records Golan’s dissertation, Scientific expert testimony in Anglo-American courts, 1782-1923, completed in 1997.
The authority cites the same dissertation, dated fall 1997, under Tal Golan.

notes: Exact dissertation and degree year connect the authority to the UCSD faculty member and the AHA doctorate.

who: Gerald J. Goodwin, historian at the University of Houston and coauthor of A History of the United States.

evidence.says: Houston’s dissertation list names Gerald Goodwin as advisor of Howard Beeth’s 1984 dissertation, Outside Agitators in Southern History.
Houston’s Faculty Vita Records collection, covering 1960–1990, includes a file for Gerald J. Goodwin.
The authority cites A History of the U.S. (1980 onward), identifying Gerald J. Goodwin at the University of Houston.

notes: The authority’s name and Houston affiliation agree with the university’s faculty and advisor records.

who: History supervisor recorded by AHA at the University of Delaware in 1978–1980, with a Yale PhD in 1969; fuller identity unverified.

evidence.says: The John Dennis Gould authority describes a professor of economic history at Victoria University of Wellington, appointed in 1963, following work at Auckland.
The John M. Gould authority cites Drexel’s School of Education faculty directory and research in change leadership, curriculum redesign and technology in learning.

notes: The supplied authorities were checked, but none could be connected to the Delaware supervisor or Yale doctorate. Several describe demonstrably different careers; the remaining sparse records do not justify a group-wide no.

who: Historian of early modern Europe at Loyola University Chicago, 1967–1999; PhD Chicago 1966.

evidence.says: AHA’s memorial records his Chicago doctorate in 1966, Loyola service from 1967 to 1999, and authorship of Empire and Sovereignty.
The Hanns Gross authority cites his Empire and Sovereignty, published in 1973 and a later edition.

notes: Matching work, degree and Loyola career establish the candidate’s identity during both students’ dissertation years.

who: John Randolph Hubbard, historian of Britain and USC president during 1970–1980; history PhD Texas 1950.

evidence.says: USC records his history PhD from Texas in 1950, arrival as provost in 1969, and election as president in 1970.
The authority for John R. (John Randolph) Hubbard explicitly identifies USC’s provost in 1969–1970, president in 1970–1980 and professor of history in 1980–1990.

notes: The authority’s USC career and the independently recorded Texas doctorate match the supervisor’s institution, period and own PhD.

who: Historian of Britain and the British empire at Boston College; history PhD UC Berkeley 2010.

evidence.says: Boston College lists Ismay as a History associate professor, with a Berkeley PhD and research in Britain and the British empire.
The dissertation title page identifies Penelope Gwynn Ismay, Trust Among Strangers, PhD in History, Berkeley, fall 2010.
The authority cites Trust among strangers (2018), identifying Penelope Ismay at Boston College.

notes: The authority names the students’ institution; faculty and dissertation records confirm the field and exact doctorate.

who: Historian of Romania at the University of Arizona; PhD Indiana University Bloomington 1969.

evidence.says: The author directory gives an Indiana Bloomington PhD in 1969 and Arizona history appointments beginning in 1967.
The 1990 book’s author statement identifies Frederick Kellogg as associate professor of history at the University of Arizona.
The authority identifies Frederick Kellogg through Rumanian nationalism and European diplomacy, 1866-1878 (1969), and his work on Romanian diplomatic history.

notes: The authority’s historical field and 1969 dissertation agree with the Arizona historian’s doctorate and career.
